title: Bose–Hubbard NQS: periodic 2D benchmarks and sector leakage

slides.title:
Bose–Hubbard NQS
Periodic 2D systems
slides.subtitle: ED construction • supervised representation • small-system VMC

slides.title: What are we testing?
lines: 1. Is the Bose–Hubbard ED construction correct?
2. Can basic NQS reproduce its ground state with supervision?
3. Does stochastic VMC work on small, checkable systems?
4. What does a fixed-N fit predict in untrained sectors?
slides.footer: Building and benchmarking a physics tool. Architecture searches and optimizer rankings are separate research directions.

slides.title: Hamiltonian
lines: Periodic in both x and y (torus)
slides.footer: Main-body systems are periodic in BOTH directions; the diagram is a3×3 torus. Cylinder results remain in supporting material. All hopping bonds are unique unordered pairs; short length-two axes have one bond per pair.

slides.title: Independent ED and DMRG check
rows: Max full one-body error: max bond256
slides.footer: Both axes periodic; N=9, cutoff4, t=1, U=16.74. DMRG uses a periodic Hamiltonian with an open-chain MPS representation. Requested maximum bond dimensions128 and256 are checked against ED; the physical boundaries are never opened.

slides.title: Density and nearest-neighbor coherence
lines: C is a chosen set of physical lattice sites; α denotes x or y.
Eα contains unique unordered nearest-neighbor bonds along α, including wraps.
Main3×3 torus: C = all nine sites; |Bx(C)| = |By(C)| = 9.
slides.footer: A bond belongs to Bα(C) only when BOTH endpoints lie in C. Each physical edge is counted once. Coherence is a one-body correlation, not <n_i n_j>. At fixed N, <b_i>=0 and sum_i rho_i=N; uniform density alone does not establish superfluidity.

slides.title: ED ground state: density and coherence
slides.footer: Actual3×3-torus ED ground state: N=9, cutoff4, t=1, U=16.74. Full19,855-state sums; site i=yLx+x. Translation symmetry gives rho_i=1; numerical roundoff is not a density texture. The right panel is the complete one-body matrix, with diagonal Gii=rho_i. Nearest-neighbor averages include all nine bonds per direction; nonzero coherence alone does not establish thermodynamic order.

slides.title: Five basic ansatzes
slides.footer: All five ansatzes represent real positive amplitudes for the untwisted hopping model.

slides.title: Supervised objective
lines: Log-MSE is primary; infidelity refinement is a separate diagnostic.
slides.footer: Main fits use Adam + log-MSE over the chosen particle sector only. Reported overlaps and energies are checked against the raw ED ground vector. Unseen particle-number sectors never enter this loss.

slides.title: Can basic NQS fit the ED state?
slides.footer: ALL results are periodic in both axes. Adam + normalized log-MSE; checkpoint selected by log-MSE. Four neural fits reach Fabs≥0.9999 on2×3 and≥0.99 on3×3. Width32, actual trained primary fits. RBM tiny fit20000updates, others10000; Jastrow is a physical baseline.

slides.title: Supervised fits: local observables
slides.footer: Exact CANONICAL ED and NQS expectations, not MC. Density is compared SITE BY SITE; its global mean is fixed to1. D=<n(n−1)> is an onsite factorial moment. Gx/Gy average all nine unique bonds per direction, including periodic wraps.

slides.title: Supervised states: density and coherence
slides.footer: 3×3 torus, N=9, cutoff4. Full fixed-sector enumeration for ED and each supervised NQS: no Monte Carlo. Left: all nine site densities minus ED. Right: all18 unique NN bond coherences minus ED, ordered x then y with wraps included. These residuals measure state approximation error.

slides.title: Variational Monte Carlo
lines: Equilibrate fresh walkers before updates; assess frozen checkpoints.
slides.footer: Retained configurations are correlated. Proposal spacing, burn-in, independent evaluation chains and time-block statistics are recorded.

slides.title: Small-system VMC versus ED
slides.footer: 2×3 torus, N=6, cutoff4, 426 states. ED E/t=-2.581089512. Fresh initialization;500 stochastic SR+nativeSGD updates, no ED labels or supervised warm start. Exact final-state metrics; variance remains nonzero.

slides.title: VMC trajectory and independent checks
slides.footer: Curves are noisy training Monte Carlo estimates before each update, not exact energies or monotone descent. Exact final metrics and frozen321/654 measurements are assessed separately. One fit per model is a proof of principle, not an architecture ranking.

slides.title: Frozen sampler versus exact state
slides.footer: Both evaluation seeds are retained; neither selects the training checkpoint. Error estimates are conditional on mixing and stationarity, not confidence intervals or proof of equilibration.

slides.title: VMC states: density and coherence
slides.footer: 2×3 torus, N=6, cutoff4. Exact saved-NQS expectations use all426 configurations; frozenMC654 crosses show independent sampled estimates ± conditionalSEM. ED is also enumerated exactly. Both seeds appear in the appendix. Three x and six y bonds: this short rectangle need not have Gx=Gy.

slides.title: Criticality and finite-size validation
lines: A closing gap weakens energy as a certificate of fidelity.
Gaplessness does not imply that variational Monte Carlo must fail.
Finite tori require their own checks before bulk claims.
slides.footer: Bound assumes a unique ground state and a normalized trial state in the same sector. Use total expectation energy, not energy density or one noisy MC estimate. Carleo & Troyer, Science355,602(2017), demonstrate finite-size NQS-VMC at criticality; no thermodynamic guarantee follows.

slides.title: Neutral gap: excitation at fixed N
slides.footer: Neutral means no particle is added or removed: E1(N) is the first excited energy in the same sector as E0(N). This is an ED spectral gap, not a neural-network metric. The charge gap E0(N+1)+E0(N−1)−2E0(N) is different. Both eigenpairs are checked by residuals; these finite clusters do not establish an infinite-system gap.
slides.subtitle: $\Delta_N=E_1(N)-E_0(N)$: lowest two eigenvalues of the SAME fixed-N Hamiltonian.

slides.title: Fixed-N fit and untrained particle sectors
lines: Training sees only N0=9; the raw network also returns values outside it.
slides.footer: Nine sites with local occupations0,…,4 allow N=0,…,36. Full probabilities normalize over all5^9 configurations; PW conditions only on W. The physical canonical state is zero outside N0; the raw exp(f) generally is not. Raw leakage tests an untrained extension, not the particle numbers visited by canonical VMC.

slides.title: Measured raw sector weights
slides.footer: Same supervised3×3-torus primary fits, trained ONLY at N=9. All5^9 configurations are enumerated. LEFT: raw globally normalized probabilities, with dots at N=9 and tails below10^-9 clipped. RIGHT: the same raw weights conditioned on N=7,…,11. High canonical overlap need not imply large raw mass at N=9; these are different normalizations.

slides.title: Leakage and within-sector accuracy
slides.footer: 3×3 TORUS, cutoff4. Nearby leakage sums GLOBAL probabilities of N=7,8,10,11; total leakage sums every N≠9. These are not window-conditional probabilities. High canonical overlap can coexist with large raw leakage; no universal architecture ranking follows.

slides.title: Fixed-sector data cannot fix leakage
lines: All canonical fits and observables stay unchanged.
RBM visible biases implement a number tilt within the same family.
Neighboring-sector weights depend on an untrained extension.
slides.footer: This is an exact postprocessing control, not a claim that each finite neural architecture realizes every h. Examples: h=a(N−N0) tilts sectors; h=−lambda(N−N0)^2 suppresses both sides. Distinct projected particle-number states are orthogonal; these weights are not transition probabilities.

slides.title: Same canonical state, different leakage
slides.footer: Algebraic reweighting of the SAME measured logZN, without new inference, fitting or checkpoint selection. h(9)=0 throughout. Changes in raw full-space weight cannot be detected by any fixed-N9 fitting metric.

slides.title: Enforce the intended physical support
lines: No retraining is needed; canonical predictions are preserved.
A number penalty on fixed-N training samples is identically zero.
slides.footer: Restricting sampled configurations is standard for U(1) conservation in canonical VMC (Pei & Clark2024). Learning an off-sector penalty requires off-sector examples or sampling; explicit output masks can instead impose it directly. Raw leakage is an extension diagnostic, not an error of projected VMC or proof of wasted capacity.

slides.title: What this benchmark establishes
lines: ED: independent physics and numerical checks agree.
Supervision: basic neural ansatzes approximate the ED state.
VMC: validate stochastic optimization on small finite clusters.
Raw neighboring-sector amplitudes are a separate diagnostic.
Exact number projection enforces the intended physical support.
slides.footer: Large-system critical performance and improved NQS optimization remain separate questions. Neither leakage nor a finite-budget VMC plateau by itself proves an expressiveness limit.

slides.title: Supporting calculations
slides.subtitle: SR derivation, sampling checks and cylinder context

slides.title: Validate the ED construction
rows: U n(n−1)/2 diagonal and fixed-N chemical shift
Canonical basis, wraps, no self/doubled bonds
slides.footer: 15 ED-specific tests pass; the periodic single-particle result is checked separately. Independent operator construction tests the physics conventions; solver residual alone would not validate the Hamiltonian.

slides.title: Exact measurement on small systems
lines: Enumerate all fixed-N configurations for BOTH ED and the saved NQS.
slides.footer: These are full-sector expectations without sampling error. Off-diagonal matrix elements connect occupations by one boson hop and include the bosonic square-root factor. Exact saved-NQS error versus ED measures the state approximation; it does not test the sampler.

slides.title: Monte Carlo: density and coherence
slides.footer: Row-action convention: the sampled configuration is the bra; the connected ket removes one boson at i and adds it at j. Set R=0 unless n_i>0 and n_j<Nmax. Wavefunctions here are real and positive; each hop preserves total N. D_i is a factorial moment; Var(n_i)=D_i+rho_i−rho_i².

slides.title: Frozen measurements and error bars
lines: Freeze the checkpoint; sample fixed-N chains with no parameter updates.
Form each site/bond average PER SAMPLE, retaining its covariance.
Block consecutive times within each walker before pooling block means.
slides.footer: Frozen seeds321/654 are both retained; plots use predeclared654. Small2×3 cases:64walkers ×512retained steps, burn4096 proposals/walker, thin8, block64; new6×4 rows:128walkers, thin16. A proposal is one local move attempt, not a lattice sweep. SEM assumes stationarity, independent walkers and sufficiently decorrelated blocks; it is not proof of mixing. Larger NQS cylinders use MC versus DMRG, not enumeration.

slides.title: Sector normalizations and overlap
lines: $\ell_{\rm near}=\sum_{N\in W,\ N\ne N_0}P_{\rm full}(N),\qquad \ell_{\rm full}=1-P_{\rm full}(N_0)$
Ffull compares the raw full-space state to zero-embedded canonical ED.
slides.footer: All overlaps are absolute and unsquared. Full means the finite cutoff0..4 basis; it does not mean unbounded Fock space. PW is conditional on the nearby window and cannot substitute for Pfull in either leakage definition.

slides.title: Nearby untrained sectors: two diagnostics
slides.footer: Both panels use UNPROJECTED3×3-torus outputs. LEFT renormalizes over N=7,…,11 only, not the full space or the physical fixed-N state. RIGHT removes sector multiplicity using w̄N=ZN/dN; d7=6,030 and d11=48,879. Dividing by w̄9 removes the overall amplitude scale.

slides.title: Ridge SR: definitions
slides.footer: M counts retained configurations, not independent samples. P counts trainable parameters. These formulas use the real, positive-amplitude ansatz and fixed-N sector.

slides.title: Imaginary time and the metric
lines: SR matches a linearized variational step to imaginary-time evolution.
slides.footer: First-order wavefunction and second-order distance expansion; Monte Carlo estimates replace expectations. S is the real quantum geometric metric, not the energy Hessian.

slides.title: Ridge SR as least squares
lines: The code assigns d as the gradient to native SGD.
slides.footer: The Euclidean parameter penalty stabilizes ill-conditioned directions and changes the step. No Adam is applied after SR; the learning-rate convention absorbs the energy-gradient factor of two.

slides.title: The exact sample-space solve
lines: Same full batch and ridge; use the smaller dense system.
slides.footer: For positive tau, this is the same regularized direction in exact arithmetic. Centered sample rank is at most min(P,M−1). No additional sample, parameter or rank truncation is introduced.

slides.title: What ridge does to each mode
lines: Small-curvature directions are smoothly damped, not estimated reliably by assumption.
slides.footer: The ridge trades step fidelity for stability. A small sampled linearized step does not guarantee a small nonlinear wavefunction change or successful optimization.

slides.title: Relation to published MinSR
lines: Our ridge uses 1/(λ+τ); the optional comparison uses the published soft filter.
slides.footer: Chen & Heyl, Nature Physics 20, 1476–1481 (2024), doi:10.1038/s41567-024-02566-1, Methods Eqs.20–23. Zero modes require explicit handling; actual SGD update is −ηd.

slides.title: Cost, storage and precision
rows: Model derivatives may originate in float32
slides.footer: Costs exclude sampling and neural differentiation. Linear in P only at fixed M in the sample-space branch. Same-batch CPU audit: P=3681, M=256, primal/dual relative direction error 1.5×10⁻¹¹; not a long-run convergence proof.

slides.title: Comparison with the 1D routine
lines: $\tau=\lambda_{\rm sum}/M\quad\text{matches ridge units; centering still differs.}$
1D CPU code solves in float64; 2D solves on the training device in float64.
slides.footer: Changes to centering, ridge units and device are separate from Jacobian vectorization. The user accepted the 2D formulation. Gauge shifts can affect parameter differences without changing normalized-state tangents.

slides.title: Small-system SR comparison
slides.subtitle: 3×3 cylinder, RBM64; M=128, P=2989; one SGD step, η=0.001
slides.settings_note:
Ridge: τ = 0.001
MinSR: relative cutoff 10⁻¹², absolute cutoff 0
slides.footer: Same weights and 128 IID samples from current NQS probabilities. Energies evaluated over all 19,855 configurations (ED ground E/t = −4.385697). One batch and one step illustrate the methods, not convergence or superiority.

occupation_embedding(n)

One token per physical site
Global attention over sites

TransformerEncoderLayer(
    d_model=32, nhead=1,
    dim_feedforward=64,
    dropout=0,
    activation="relu")

Mean pool → linear scalar
items.note: Width32 matches the periodic primary fits.

slides.footer: No phase/sign output is needed here. Neither mean pooling nor learned positions guarantee lattice translation symmetry.

slides.title: Compare: 4×4 cylinder
slides.footer: Progress snapshot: confirmation seed 654 when available, screening seed 321 otherwise. A neural pass requires both seeds and all four targets. Jastrow is a fixed baseline, exempt from that gate.

slides.title: Compare: 6×4 cylinder
slides.footer: 6×4 CYLINDER: open x, periodic y; N=24, cutoff4, U/t=16.74. All rows use frozen seed654; gap is relative energy/site error to the same chi128 DMRG reference. Neural pass requires BOTH seeds: whole E/site and central-strip density/Gx/Gy point AND precision targets. Jastrow is the original displacement baseline, exempt from the neural gate. Budgets differ; no architecture ranking. J/RBM first attempts became nonfinite; selected fresh retries use smaller steps and fixed larger ridge (protocols retained).

slides.title: Periodic VMC: local observables
slides.footer: BOTH frozen seeds321/654 retained; exact refers to full426-state expectation of that NQS, while ED is the reference ground state. D=<n(n−1)>; sample composites precede blocking. Errors are conditionalSEM, not confidence intervals or mixing proofs.

slides.title: Convolution + Transformer in 2D

items.name: Local features
items.note: 32 channels. Periodic padding on both axes in these tests.

items.name: Global attention
items.note: One encoder block; width32, FF64, ReLU, dropout0. No positional embeddings.

items.name: Scalar head
items.note: Physical order i=yLx+x. Dense head can break translation symmetry.

slides.footer: 2D generalization of the existing 1D ConvTransformer: Conv1d becomes a boundary-aware Conv2d, followed by the same attention/flatten/dense pattern. Dropout is set to0 for deterministic VMC. Local convolution and global attention provide complementary features; improved accuracy is an empirical question, not guaranteed by this structure.

slides.title: Hybrid: supervised ED benchmarks
slides.footer: Width32; one four-head block. Adam + normalized log-MSE,10000 updates, seed123; saved by log-MSE. Raw-ED checks in CPUfloat64. Both axes periodic, cutoff4. Tiny gate: Fabs≥0.9999 and δE/site≤0.001t; 3×3 working gate: Fabs≥0.99. A single fixed-budget fit tests this setup, not universal capacity.

slides.title: Hybrid: fresh small-system VMC
slides.footer: ED E/t=-2.581089512. Fresh seed123;500 stochastic ridge-SR + nativeSGD updates, M=1024; no ED labels or warm start. Exact full426-state final expectations. Hybrid runs GPUfloat32/TF32off with float64 SR; earlier FC/Conv run CPUfloat64. Different parameter counts and arithmetic: this is a functionality check, not a controlled ranking.

slides.title: Hybrid: frozen observable checks
slides.footer: BOTH frozen evaluation seeds retained, CPUfloat64,64walkers ×512retained steps, block64. D=<n(n−1)>; Gx/Gy average the three/six unique NN bonds. Composite each sample BEFORE blocking to retain covariance. Errors are max(blockSEM,between-chainSEM), conditional on mixing; exact-state error and MC scatter are separate.

slides.title: Hybrid: density and NN coherence
slides.footer: 2×3 fully periodic, fixed N=6. Curves are exact expectations of the saved VMC state minus ED; crosses are frozenMC654 ± conditionalSEM. Includes periodic wraps and Hermitian bond estimators. Pointwise density, rather than its conserved mean, tests the learned profile.

slides.title: Hybrid: raw neighboring-sector weights
slides.footer: Same supervised3×3 torus checkpoint, trained ONLY at N=9: F9=0.999577, raw Pfull(9)=0.0057816. All5^9 cutoff configurations enumerated; left-panel tails below10^-9 are clipped. Right panel renormalizes ONLY over N=7,…,11. Raw leakage is unconstrained extension, not canonical VMC contamination; exact number projection enforces physical support without retraining.
